terms.gloss: open the way (to), pave the way for
terms.grammar: phrase: sibi viam facere, to make one’s way
evidence: Vell. 2.3.4: lātissimē ēvagandī sibi viam facere, of precedents (Lewis & Short s.v. ēvagor)
Traupman p. 105: to pave the way to, viam faciō ad (+ acc.)
terms.comment: The passage speaks of bad precedents that “make themselves a way” to spread.

sources: Lewis & Short: via
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 105, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
